title: Recursion
summary: A function that calls itself to solve smaller versions of a problem. Elegant for tree-shaped data (like the instance hierarchy); needs a base case to stop.

details.heading: Stack depth
details.body: Each self-call adds a stack frame. Deep recursion (thousands of levels) overflows the stack. For Roblox's instance tree this is rarely a problem; for large generated data, prefer explicit loops.

details.heading: Local functions and recursion
details.body: `local function f() f() end` works — the name is in scope inside its own body. Forward-declare only when the function is a value assigned later.

explanation.whatItIs: A function solving a problem by solving a smaller copy of the same problem, until the problem is trivial (the *base case*).
explanation.whyItExists: Some data is naturally self-similar: folder hierarchies, nested tables, family trees. Recursive code mirrors that shape.
whenToUse: Walking the instance hierarchy (though `GetDescendants()` usually replaces this)
whenNotToUse: When a built-in already does it: prefer `GetDescendants()` over hand-rolled hierarchy walking
When depth is unbounded or huge — an explicit stack/queue loop is safer
When a simple loop is just as clear
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
printTree(model)
  print(model)
  for each child:
      printTree(child)    -- same job, smaller target

-- stops when a child has no children (base case)
```
tips: Write the base case FIRST, then the recursive step
Every recursive call must move toward the base case, or you loop forever
Roblox provides GetDescendants() — reach for recursion when you also need custom logic per level
commonMistakes: Missing/incorrect base case → infinite recursion → stack overflow error
Forgetting that each call is independent — locals don't accumulate unless you pass them as arguments
Recursing through workspace every frame for something GetDescendants could cache

examples.title: Walk the hierarchy with custom logic
examples.code:
local function tagAllParts(instance)
    if instance:IsA("BasePart") then
        instance:SetAttribute("Scanned", true)
    end
    for _, child in instance:GetChildren() do
        tagAllParts(child)   -- recurse into each child
    end
end

tagAllParts(workspace)
-- (For pure collection, workspace:GetDescendants() is simpler.)

examples.title: Classic: factorial
examples.code:
local function factorial(n)
    if n <= 1 then return 1 end   -- base case
    return n * factorial(n - 1)   -- smaller problem
end

print(factorial(5))   --> 120
